### Day 282: Acts 22:22–29
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-282-acts-22-2229.html
Passage: Acts 22:22-29
Points:
- True Christian success is measured by faithful obedience to God rather than measurable human results.
- The Jerusalem mob turned against Paul because their desire for national superiority outweighed spiritual truth.
- God gave Paul the platform to speak to his persecutors, planting seeds that the Holy Spirit could bring to mind later.
- God providentially prepared Paul before birth with Roman citizenship, using his unique background to protect him.
- Paul was willing to endure hostility and pour himself out because he was confident in the One who called him.

### Read the Bible: Genesis 23, Matthew 22, Nehemiah 12, and Acts 22
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-23-matthew-22-nehemiah-12-acts-22/
Passage: Acts 22:22-29
Points:
- The crowd listened peacefully to Paul's testimony until he declared God's mission to the Gentiles.
- The mob erupted because Paul's mission challenged their national identity and presumed exclusive ownership of God.
- Treating God as the exclusive domain of one culture distorts Scripture and quenches the missionary impulse.
- Paul asserted his Roman citizenship rather than accepting a flogging to establish a legal precedent protecting believers.
- Appealing to his civil rights served to show that Christianity is legally vindicated and not politically subversive.
